defines the journey.
Located in Kew, Kneller Hall Junior School is a co-educational school for children aged 4–11.
Where each child can be the hero of their own adventure
Life at Kneller Hall Junior is busy, joyful and full of possibility. Children are encouraged to follow their curiosity, discover their passions and embrace new challenges with confidence. Along the way, they develop the independence, resilience and love of learning that will shape them throughout their time here and prepare them for the next stage of their adventure.
Welcome from our Head
At Kneller Hall Junior, we believe the primary years are some of the most important in a child’s education. From Reception through to Year 6, we provide a nurturing, ambitious and enriching environment where children develop confidence, independence and a genuine love of learning.Our approach goes beyond academic achievement. We encourage children to be curious, creative and courageous, giving them the opportunity to discover their individual strengths, explore their interests and embrace new challenges. With dedicated teaching, a broad and balanced curriculum and a strong sense of community, every child is supported to make the most of their time at Kneller Hall.By the end of Year 6, our pupils leave as confident, capable and curious young people, ready to take their next steps with enthusiasm and self-belief.
THE Kneller EXPERIENCE
Pastoral Care
THE Kneller APPROACH

The Radnor Difference
Why Families Choose Kneller Hall Junior
A child’s early years at school shape confidence, curiosity and a love of learning. At Kneller Hall Junior, we believe education should do more than prepare children for exams it should help them discover what they are capable of.We encourage pupils to ask questions, try new things and grow in confidence through a wide range of opportunities both inside and outside the classroom. With passionate teachers and a strong sense of community, children are supported to thrive academically and personally.When a child joins Kneller Hall, they become part of a school where character, curiosity and confidence matter just as much as achievement.

pageCache.pageTitle: Head's Welcome | Private School | Radnor House Prep School
pageCache.text:
Head’s welcome
A Welcome from our Headteacher
Radnor House Prep does things differently. There is no narrow focus on the 11+. Instead, we prioritise curiosity, confidence and a genuine love of learning, giving pupils the space to explore, question and think for themselves.What sets the school apart is not just what happens in lessons, but everything around them the energy as pupils arrive, the focus when ideas take hold, and the laughter across the playground.Every child is treated as an individual, deliberately. Our teachers understand how each pupil thinks and shape their teaching accordingly. We call it “stretch without stress”: high expectations, real challenge, and the support to succeed without losing the enjoyment of learning.We work closely with our families to build a strong community around each child, ensuring every pupil leaves ready for a seamless transition into Year 7 at our senior school, Radnor House, soon to be Kneller Hall – confident and ready for what comes next.Kindness, respect and strong relationships underpin it all. They define the culture.
Who We Are
We create opportunities for every child to thrive, both inside and outside the classroom. Our environment is energetic, supportive and kind, where pupils feel encouraged to take part, challenge themselves and grow in confidence.
Through a broad and balanced experience, children develop curiosity, resilience and a genuine enthusiasm for learning, preparing them to embrace new challenges with independence and a strong sense of self.

pageCache.pageTitle: Ethos and Values | Prep School | Radnor House Prep School
pageCache.text:
our ethos and values
what makes our school
Our values are not simply statements, but a lived part of daily school life. They shape how pupils approach challenge, how they treat one another, and how they grow in confidence and character. Consistent, purposeful and quietly embedded, they create a culture where expectations are understood, relationships are strong, and every child is supported to develop both academically and personally.Time beyond lessons is equally valued, with opportunities to play, socialise and take part in a wide range of activities. By the end of the day, pupils leave not only with new knowledge, but with growing confidence, independence and enthusiasm for learning.
Respect
Respect is the foundation of how we operate. It shapes how pupils treat one another, how they engage with their teachers, and how they carry themselves within the wider community. It is not enforced through rules alone, but embedded through expectation, in behaviour, in language, and in the way people show up for each other every day.
Resilience
Resilience is developed through challenge, not avoidance. Pupils are encouraged to take risks, to try, to fail, and to try again. Through this, they build the confidence to face difficulty with composure and determination. Setbacks are not seen as barriers, but as part of a process that strengthens character over time.
Reflection
Reflection is a deliberate part of daily life. Pupils are encouraged to think about their actions, their learning, and their progress. This builds self-awareness, accountability, and the ability to make better decisions. It ensures that growth is not left to chance, but shaped with intention and clarity.
The Dukes Family
We are proud to be part of Dukes Education – a family of schools brought together by a shared belief in doing education properly. Founded in 2015, Dukes connects schools through strong leadership, high standards, and a genuine commitment to the people within them. Each school remains true to its own identity, while benefiting from a wider network of expertise, opportunity and ambition. At Radnor House Prep, this means staying grounded in who we are, while giving our pupils the advantage of being part of something bigger.

pageCache.pageTitle: Pastoral Care | Prep School London | Radnor House Prep School
pageCache.text:
pastoral care
Safeguarding and Wellbeing at Radnor House Prep
How is pupil wellbeing supported day-to-day?
Our ethos is simple: every child is seen, supported, and championed as an individual. This commitment is reflected in our structured pastoral system, which begins with the positioning of a dedicated member of staff for every class – whose role is to provide consistent pastoral support. Class Teacher in the Lower School (Reception–Year 2) and the Form Tutor in the Upper School (Year 3–Year 6). The Class Teacher or Form Tutor is the primary contact for families and the lead supporter for each pupil. They register the class in the morning, monitor children throughout the day as they move to specialist lessons, and respond promptly to any observations or concerns, ensuring each child receives the care and guidance they need. Wellbeing is further strengthened through regular discussions at weekly staff meetings, as well as a robust internal system to log, track, and monitor pupil welfare. Pupil voice is central to our approach. Children are encouraged to share their opinions and experiences, whether on school-wide matters or in private conversations with trusted staff members. This ensures that every pupil feels heard, valued, and supported. The school also has a trained Emotional Literacy Support Assistant (ELSA) based on site and available for all our pupils.
What systems are in place for safeguarding?
A strong and robust safeguarding culture underpins everything at Radnor House Prep School. For pupils, safeguarding is an integral part of school life. Regular reminders about communication channels are shared visually around the school and reinforced through assembly themes. Pupils’ understanding is further supported through high-quality teaching in the PSHEE & RSHE curriculum, which includes guidance on online safety, and strengthened further through their strong and positive relationships with their teachers. The school also works closely with external specialists, including the NSPCC, who deliver targeted assemblies and workshops to enhance pupils’ learning and awareness. Our safeguarding leadership is both experienced and proactive. The school has a dedicated Designated Safeguarding Lead and Deputy, supported by a Safeguarding Governor from Dukes Education. Safeguarding training is embedded into weekly staff meetings and more in-depth training is planned regularly for all staff, ensuring that every member of staff remains alert, informed, and confident in their responsibilities. Safer recruitment practices are rigorously followed when appointing new staff and continue throughout induction and probation. Clear expectations are reinforced through the employee handbook, regular staff meeting agenda areas, and ensuring a consistently safe and supportive environment for all.
What support is available for pupils with additional needs?
As a mainstream, inclusive, and non-selective school, we celebrate and support a broad range of abilities within every class. High expectations are maintained for all pupils, with carefully planned differentiation and scaffolding embedded in teaching to support progress and achievement. Our dedicated team of teachers uses the school’s assessment framework – combining formal assessments and in-class observations – to tailor planning and teaching, ensuring that every child is appropriately challenged and supported. Where beneficial, small-group interventions are offered in areas such as spelling, number foundations in Maths, and handwriting, among others. The school has a small, specialist SEND department led by a trained and experienced SENDCo. For pupils with an EHCP or formal diagnosis, provision is carefully reviewed during the admissions process to ensure the school has the capacity and resources to cater for specific needs and requirements. For pupils with an EHCP or formal diagnosis, the SENDCo oversees tailored support and resources to meet individual needs.

pageCache.pageTitle: Teaching and Learning | Radnor House Prep School
pageCache.text:
Teaching and learning
Our curriculum
At Radnor House Prep, learning is shaped by expertise, intention and high expectations. Our teachers create an environment where pupils are challenged, supported and encouraged to think for themselves. The result is more than strong outcomes. it is confident, capable pupils, prepared for the next stage and ready to take it on.This foundation is reinforced through a broad and balanced curriculum, where academic rigour sits alongside creativity, sport and personal development. Pupils are given the opportunity to explore their strengths, develop resilience and take ownership of their learning building the confidence and character that carry forward into senior school and beyond.
A Broad and Balanced Curriculum for Every Stage of their journey
Academic Foundations
English, mathematics, science and humanities — building strong knowledge, confidence and depth of understanding.
STEAM and Innovation
Coding, robotics and design-led learning that develops problem-solving, creativity and technical confidence.
Creative and Performing Arts
Music, art and drama that encourage expression, confidence and performance.
Sport and Physical Education
A strong sporting culture developing teamwork, resilience and a lifelong enjoyment of being active.
Specialist subjects
At Radnor House Prep, we go beyond the basics – offering a rich, varied specialist curriculum that ensures our pupils flourish academically, creatively and physically. Our programme is designed to help every child discover their strengths, build confidence, and develop the wide-ranging skills they’ll need for future learning and life.
We have a strong STEAM (Science, Technology, Engineering, Arts and Mathematics) strand running through much of our curriculum, giving pupils the opportunity to learn through hands-on, real-life projects. This even includes lessons in robotics and electronics — allowing children to build digital literacy and apply it creatively.Our teaching also embraces modern tools: iPads are used across the curriculum to support learning and students are able to get hands-on with augmented reality (AR) and virtual reality (VR) to prepare them for a digital world. Whether working collaboratively or independently, pupils learn design, problem-solving and innovation — skills central to STEM and to navigating an increasingly technological future.
In the linguistic strand, pupils study English and French – developing both strong literacy skills and an early appreciation for language learning.Our humanities programme includes Geography, History and Religious Studies (RS), giving children a rounded understanding of the world, its cultures, and its past — fostering awareness, empathy and informed global citizenship.
Music, Art, and Drama are key components of our curriculum’s “Creative & Performing Arts” strand — offering children the chance to express themselves, build confidence and explore different forms of creativity. Through creative arts, children develop aesthetic appreciation, self-expression and collaboration. Whether painting, performing or making music, pupils grow their creative voices across the years.
Physical activity and sport play a central role in life at Radnor Prep. Our programme aims to develop teamwork, leadership, resilience and a love of healthy activity.Pupils have access to PE, Games and outdoor activity – whether through structured sport, outdoor learning or adventurous activities — promoting physical development, well-being and a balanced lifestyle.Our approach reflects a belief in holistic education: just as important as academic success is the development of physical confidence, resilience and a sense of fun.
Alongside core academic and specialist subjects, Radnor Prep places a strong emphasis on life skills: emotional intelligence, digital literacy, data literacy, global citizenship, empathy, curiosity, and entrepreneurship are woven into daily learning.Pupils have the opportunity to work towards the Dukes Young Leaders award — a recognition of their growth not just academically but as thoughtful, responsible members of a community.Our inclusive and supportive ethos ensures that children of all backgrounds and abilities are welcomed. Specialist teaching is in place from the earliest years, including in computing, sport, music, French and art.Through regular workshops, clubs, trips and co-curricular activities, we encourage pupils to explore beyond the classroom — discovering new passions and developing a broad, balanced set of interests.
Digital Learning
Pupil wellbeing, purpose and ambition remain at the heart of everything we do. Alongside strong academic foundations, technology is introduced carefully and intentionally to support creativity, collaboration and deeper engagement with learning. From Years 3–6, pupils use iPads where they genuinely add value across a range of subjects. They are particularly effective within STEAM lessons, where technology supports design, creativity and problem-solving, allowing pupils to explore ideas in more dynamic and engaging ways.Technology is used with balance and purpose, ensuring pupils develop confidence and independence without losing the importance of hands-on learning and real-world interaction.

A day in the life at radnor
a unique Experience
At Radnor House Prep, our curriculum is designed to challenge, inspire and support every pupil to achieve their full potential. We combine strong academic foundations with a broad and engaging programme of learning, ensuring children develop not only knowledge and skills, but confidence, curiosity and a genuine love of learning. Each subject is carefully taught to build understanding over time, while giving pupils the opportunity to think independently, ask questions and explore ideas in depth.
A School Day That Feels Balanced, Purposeful And Full Of Energy
At Radnor House Prep, each day is carefully structured to balance focus, creativity and time to explore. From the moment pupils arrive, classrooms are purposeful and engaging, with lessons designed to challenge thinking and encourage collaboration. Alongside strong foundations in core subjects, pupils benefit from specialist teaching in areas such as music, sport and STEAM, adding depth and variety to their learning. Time beyond lessons is equally valued, with opportunities to play, socialise and take part in a wide range of activities. By the end of the day, pupils leave not only with new knowledge, but with growing confidence, independence and enthusiasm for learning.

Admissions process
Admissions
We are delighted that you are considering Radnor House Prep School for your child.
Our Admissions Manager will be pleased to answer any questions you may have, provide further information about the school, or help you arrange a visit to see Radnor House Prep in action. Choosing the right school is an important decision, and our admissions team is here to guide families through every stage of the process. From arranging an initial visit to discussing the best entry point for your child, we aim to make joining our community as straightforward and welcoming as possible.
Phone: 020 3869 5871Email: office@rhprep.com
Admissions process
Registration is open from birth and we encourage families to register their child as early as possible. Our main point of entry is Nursery, with children typically joining Radnor House Prep in the term they turn three.
For Nursery entry, early registrants are placed on our main list and prioritised when places become available. Once the main list is full, and for entry into other year groups, applications are added to our waiting list.
Please note that registration does not guarantee the offer of a place.
Registration is open from birth, and we recommend registering your child as early as possible. Complete our online registration form to join the waiting list.
A non-refundable registration fee of £150 is required at the time of application.
Our main entry points are at Nursery (or the equivalent earliest class offered) and at any year group subject to availability. Once registered, children will be offered the next available place when one becomes available.
We regularly host Open Days and tours so families can see our school in action, meet staff, and learn about our ethos and facilities. We encourage prospective parents and children to attend if possible.
Once an offer has been made and accepted, you will be given details of the next steps to confirm your child’s place.
Start your journey
We look forward to welcoming you to the Radnor House Prep community and supporting your child’s educational journey.

pageCache.pageTitle: Fees | Prep School London | Radnor House Prep School
pageCache.text:
Fees
Termly and Admissions Fees
Termly Fees 2026/27
The fees for Reception to Year 6 are £8,221 per termThese fees include lunch, breakfast and a mid-morning snack. Please note that all fees are inclusive of all applicable taxes (including VAT) or applicable levies.
Admissions fees
A non-refundable registration fee of £180 is payable at the time of application.To accept an offer of a place, a deposit of £3,000 must be paid by the deadline specified in the offer letter. This deposit is refunded when the pupil leaves school — minus any costs for unreturned or damaged school property. If the place is not taken up after the deposit is paid, the deposit is non-refundable.
Terms and notice period
Fees are invoiced on a termly basis in advance (invoices are issued approximately four weeks before the start of term) and are payable by direct debit. A full term’s written notice must be given to the Head to avoid liability for the following term’s fee payment, should you wish to withdraw your child.
Fees and extras
Alongside termly tuition fees, families may choose from a range of optional extras to support their child’s learning and daily routine. These services are charged in addition to core fees and are invoiced termly where applicable.
Sibling Discounts
Families will be eligible for a sibling discount as follows:
• Two siblings – 5% discount applied to the fees of the second child • Three or more siblings – 10% discount applied to the fees of the second child – 5% discount applied to the fees of the third child and any additional siblings
Sibling discounts are applied to tuition fees only and cannot be combined with any other fee remission unless specifically agreed by the school. Sibling order is determined by age and is unaffected by the order of school enrolment. To qualify as siblings, pupils must be one of two or more biological or legally adopted children sharing one or both parents. The discount does not extend to step-siblings or other non-sibling family members.
Radnor House Prep offers wraparound care before and after school to support busy families. Breakfast is included in the morning session.
Lunch, breakfast and morning snack are included within the core school fees for all pupils from Reception to Year 6.
We offer a varied programme of clubs, enrichment and extended-day activities. Some clubs are run by external providers and may incur additional charges. A termly activities schedule with associated costs is shared with parents in advance.
Most local curriculum trips are included in the core tuition fees. Residential trips, specialist workshops or activities requiring additional transport or external providers are charged separately. Parents are informed of costs ahead of booking.
Individual music tuition is available in a variety of instruments. Lessons are delivered by visiting peripatetic teachers and are billed directly by the music tutors.
School uniform must be purchased from the designated Radnor House Prep supplier. A full uniform list and price guide are available on the school website.

pageCache.pageTitle: Life Beyond Lessons | Radnor House Prep School
pageCache.text:
Life Beyond Lessons
Learning beyond the classroom
Clubs and activities
Learning continues long after the bell rings at Radnor House Prep. Our club programme runs throughout the week, with opportunities before school, at lunchtime and after lessons. Clubs reflect the interests and curiosity of our pupils and change throughout the year. From creative projects to sport, music and technology, children are encouraged to try new things, develop their talents and enjoy time with friends.
Creative clubs give pupils space to experiment and express themselves. Activities include arts and crafts, comic book club, musical theatre, choir and film academy, allowing pupils to explore storytelling, performance and design.
Our STEAM-focused clubs encourage curiosity and problem solving. Pupils can take part in coding club, science club and technology-based activities, developing practical skills while exploring new ideas.
Sport is a lively part of the club programme, with activities such as football, netball, dodgeball, archery. These sessions encourage teamwork, confidence and a love of being active.
Some clubs focus on developing new skills or exploring personal interests. These include sewing and design, Lego and puzzle club, mindfulness sessions, cookery and touch typing.
Sports and music
Sport is a lively and enjoyable part of the school day at Radnor House Prep. Whether it’s a PE lesson, a match with another school or simply time spent practising together, pupils are encouraged to get involved and enjoy being active.Children try a range of sports as they move through the school, learning new skills and building confidence along the way. Team sports help pupils support one another, celebrate successes together and learn how to handle both winning and losing with good spirit.Most importantly, sport is about participation. We want every child to feel part of the team and to leave the field smiling.
Music is woven naturally into life at Radnor House Prep. Pupils sing together, learn instruments and have regular opportunities to perform throughout the year.Many children choose to take individual music lessons, while others enjoy being part of choirs or small groups. From practising in the music room to performing in concerts and school events, music gives pupils the chance to express themselves and grow in confidence.Whether a child is picking up an instrument for the first time or performing for an audience, music is a joyful part of school life.
Trips and Outdoor Learning
Children learn best when they are actively involved. At Radnor House Prep, trips, outdoor activities and hands-on projects form an important part of school life, helping pupils connect their learning to the world around them.Whether exploring nature, visiting places linked to their studies or taking part in practical environmental projects, pupils have opportunities to learn through experience. These activities encourage children to ask questions, work together and develop a deeper understanding of how things work beyond the classroom.Projects such as growing plants and caring for bees allow pupils to see the results of their efforts over time. Through experiences like these, children develop patience, responsibility and a greater appreciation for the natural environment.
Charity work
At Radnor House Prep, we believe that schools should play an active role within their local community. Through partnerships, charitable work and shared initiatives, we encourage pupils to develop empathy, awareness and a sense of responsibility beyond the classroom.
Supporting local charities
We are proud to be developing a relationship with Skylarks, a charity that supports children with additional needs and their families. Through this partnership, pupils will have opportunities to learn about inclusion, kindness and the importance of supporting others within the community.Working with organisations such as Skylarks allows our pupils to understand how small actions can make a meaningful difference. These experiences help children develop compassion and a wider awareness of the world around them.

pageCache.pageTitle: Pathway to Kneller Hall | Radnor House Prep School
pageCache.text:
Part of a shared future
Pathway to Kneller Hall
A clear and purposeful journey from Radnor House Prep to Kneller Hall, built on strong foundations and a proud sense of heritage. Rooted in legacy and shaped by shared values, pupils develop the confidence, independence and character to step forward ready for the next chapter.
A Future Driven by History and Heart
Kneller Hall represents an exciting new chapter for Radnor House School — bringing together a forward-thinking education within an exceptional historic setting. As we prepare to open in September 2027, we invite families to register their interest and be part of this journey from the very beginning. This is an opportunity to secure a place in a school shaped by strong values, high expectations and a clear vision for the future.
Built on History. Designed for What’s Next.
Kneller Hall marks the next chapter for Radnor House School – a modern education set within an exceptional historic setting. Built on strong foundations, our approach remains values-led, where kindness and compassion are prioritised, and where encouragement replaces pressure. With a clear sense of purpose, we are shaping an environment that challenges, supports and inspires — ready to open our new home at Kneller Hall in September 2027.Set within expansive grounds, with over half the site preserved as open green space, Kneller Hall offers a rare sense of scale and freedom. Purpose-built facilities for sport, performing arts, science and outdoor learning will sit alongside spaces designed for focus, creativity and collaboration giving pupils the opportunity to explore their interests in a setting that feels both ambitious and grounded.This is more than a new campus. It is a considered step forward combining heritage, environment and forward-thinking education to create a place where pupils can grow with confidence, develop independence, and fully engage with the opportunities around them.
HISTORY, CARRIED FORWARD
From military roots to modern education
Kneller Hall has a long-standing legacy as a place of discipline, learning and purpose. Now, as part of Dukes Education, that legacy continues reimagined through a modern, values-led approach that builds on the strong foundations of Radnor House School. This is not a departure from the past, but a continuation of it shaped by ambition, guided by experience, and driven by a clear vision for the future.
The Dukes Family
Kneller Hall is part of Dukes Education – a family of schools brought together by a shared belief in doing education properly. Founded in 2015, Dukes connects schools through strong leadership, high standards, and a genuine commitment to the people within them. Each school remains true to its own identity, while benefiting from a wider network of expertise, opportunity and ambition. At Radnor House Prep, this means staying grounded in who we are, while giving our pupils the advantage of being part of something bigger.

pageCache.pageTitle: Preparing for Senior School | Radnor House Prep School
pageCache.text:
preparing for senior school
Taking the Next Step
Preparing pupils for the transition to senior school is an important part of life at Radnor House Prep. Our approach focuses not only on academic readiness, but also on developing the confidence, independence and resilience that children need to thrive in their next stage of education.Every child’s journey is different. Our aim is to understand each pupil as an individual and help them move on to the senior school that best matches their strengths, interests and ambitions.
Strong Academic Foundations
A broad and balanced curriculum provides pupils with the knowledge and skills needed for senior school study. Through subjects such as English, mathematics, science, languages and the humanities, pupils develop strong academic habits and the ability to think independently.As they move through the upper years of prep school, pupils are increasingly encouraged to take responsibility for their learning, preparing them for the expectations of senior school.
Developing Independence
Senior school brings new opportunities and greater independence. Pupils gradually develop the organisational and study skills that support this transition, including managing homework, organising their time and approaching challenges with confidence.Teachers support pupils in building these habits step by step so that they feel well prepared and self-assured when they move on.
Guidance for Families
Choosing the right senior school is an important decision for families. Our staff work closely with parents to provide guidance and support throughout the process.This may include discussing potential school options, supporting applications and helping pupils prepare for entrance assessments or interviews where required.
A Confident Transition
Above all, our goal is for pupils to leave Radnor House Prep feeling confident about the next stage of their education. With strong academic foundations, well-developed study skills and a supportive school community behind them, pupils are ready to embrace the opportunities that senior school brings.
